clue.text: Stones one found round hotel

indicators.note: going round something means wrapping it, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: one on its own is single
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A beachcomber picks up pebbles lying around a seaside hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: SINGLE wraps around H to give SHINGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingle is a mass of small rounded pebbles, as found on many British beaches.

clue.text: Short time secured by reserve in box, say

indicators.note: something secured by another thing is held inside it

parts.note: a sub is a substitute, a reserve player
HR is the short form of hour

explanation.surface: A spell held back on the bench, in a box of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Box here is the evergreen plant used in hedging, given as an example of a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Box is an example of a shrub, a woody plant smaller than a tree.

clue.text: Drug in foreign pub not good after manufacture

indicators.note: manufacturing makes something new from raw material, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order
not good means without the abbreviation for good, so that letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A drug turns up in a bad foreign pub after it was made.
explanation.walkthrough: G is removed from the letters of foreign pub before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibuprofen is a common painkilling and anti-inflammatory medicine.

clue.text: Unexpected help in extreme part of theatre gallery?

parts.note: the gods are the highest, cheapest balcony seats in a theatre
the end is the extreme part of anything

explanation.surface: Help that arrives out of nowhere, perhaps from the farthest seats up in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The gods is the British name for a theatre's top gallery; the question mark marks the playful split.
explanation.definitionFit: A godsend is a welcome, unexpected piece of luck or help, as if sent from heaven.

clue.text: News journalist in English museum with viscount

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London
Vis is the abbreviation for viscount

explanation.surface: A reporter visits an English museum accompanied by a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: V AND A is the spelt-out name of London's V&A museum. Evan Davis is a BBC journalist and presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Evan Davis is a British broadcaster who has presented BBC news programmes such as Newsnight.

clue.text: Stupidity from unruly men in Norfolk town

indicators.note: being placed in something means going inside another word

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, England

indicators.note: unruly people refuse to stay in order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone blames local stupidity on a gang of rowdy men in a small Norfolk town.
explanation.walkthrough: Diss is a small market town in eastern England; crosswords use it often because its name is a handy word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dimness is slowness of mind, a synonym for stupidity.

clue.text: Object found by bird in drive

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside its letters

parts.note: Dr is the street-name abbreviation for drive
the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: A thing discovered by a bird on the driveway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection or show reluctance.

clue.text: Butterfly, one over realm?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large orange and black migrating butterfly
second meaning: a person ruling a kingdom

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: one placed over a realm is its ruler, not something flying over it.
explanation.definitionFit: The monarch is a well-known American butterfly, and a monarch is a sovereign ruler.

clue.text: Put away order without first number

indicators.note: without the first means the opening letter is taken away

parts.note: to neaten is to put in order
N is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A tidy-up command: put things away but leave out the first figure.
explanation.walkthrough: NEATEN loses its first N, a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been put away informally has been consumed, that is eaten.

clue.text: Tax on French ward

parts.note: sur is French for on
a ward is someone in your charge

explanation.surface: A levy on a French hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcharge is an extra charge or levy, a kind of tax.

clue.text: Approximate series of calls

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to express a figure to the nearest whole number or ten
second meaning: a doctor's or milkman's regular circuit of visits

explanation.surface: Someone estimates how many phone calls were made in a sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: To round a number is to make it approximate, and a round is a regular circuit of visits.

clue.text: A cross by big church? It's laid on floor

parts.note: taken as written
X is shaped like a cross
a minster is a large or important church, like York Minster

explanation.surface: A cross stands beside a cathedral, with a question about what lies on its floor.
explanation.walkthrough: Axminster is a Devon town famous for its carpets, so the definition is a cryptic description of a rug.
explanation.definitionFit: An Axminster is a kind of woven carpet, which is put down to cover a floor.

clue.text: Save bid for source of 9?

parts.note: save and bar both mean except, as in 'all save one'
a tender is a formal bid or offer

explanation.surface: An auction-style instruction: keep your offer back for something connected to answer 9.
explanation.walkthrough: 9-across is ROUND, here a round of drinks, which the person behind the bar pours.
explanation.definitionFit: A bartender serves the drinks, so is where a round of drinks comes from.

clue.text: Where to keep stock in tranches?

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the following word, waiting to be spotted

parts.note: the letters run consecutively in this word

explanation.surface: A financial question: where do you hold shares when they come in slices?
explanation.walkthrough: Stock means shares in the surface, but livestock in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm where cattle and other livestock are kept.

clue.text: Lawyer, very independent, entering a fine attack in legal document

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so these letters are placed within another word

parts.note: taken as written
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
a fit is a sudden attack, as of coughing
DA is a US district attorney
V is the abbreviation for very
I is the abbreviation for independent

explanation.surface: A fiercely independent lawyer gets caught up in a fine and an attack recorded in court papers.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' at the front joins the fine and the attack; only the lawyer, very and independent go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An affidavit is a written statement sworn on oath, used as evidence in court.

clue.text: Cordial, beer and a lager right off drunk

indicators.note: a drunk person is all over the place, so the letters are rearranged
right being off means the abbreviation for right is removed

parts.note: taken as written, without the and
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A pub scene: a cordial drink, beer and lager knocked back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' looks like a soft drink amid the beers, but it is the adjective meaning friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordial as an adjective means warm and friendly, much like pleasant or agreeable.

clue.text: Restrained painting technique and tone outwardly

parts.note: tempera is painting with pigment bound in egg yolk

indicators.note: outwardly points to the outside, so only the first and last letters count

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: An art critic describes a painter's method and overall tone as restrained.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperate means moderate and self-controlled, not given to excess.

clue.text: Actor endlessly to show indecision

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Nigel Havers is an English actor

explanation.surface: An actor dithers over a decision without end.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigel Havers, known for Chariots of Fire, loses his last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To haver is a mainly Scottish verb meaning to dither or hesitate.

clue.text: Little, perhaps, is on TV I like sadly, rejecting first signs of kitsch entertainment

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled
rejecting means throwing out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the first signs of words are their opening letters

parts.note: the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A grumble that what's on the TV one likes rarely includes trashy shows.
explanation.walkthrough: Little is not small here but Tasmin Little, the British violinist; 'perhaps' marks her as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmin Little is a celebrated English concert violinist, an example of the answer.

clue.text: Place to practise driving in some mountains

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a driving ..., where golfers hit balls
second meaning: a connected line of peaks

explanation.surface: A learner driver goes up into the mountains for practice.
explanation.walkthrough: Driving suggests cars, but here it is the golf shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf driving range is a practice ground, and a mountain range is a chain of peaks.

clue.text: Sanction retained by vendors exceptionally

indicators.note: being retained by words means being held inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A penalty held back by traders in exceptional cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sanction' reads as a penalty in the surface, but here it means approve.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction something is to approve it officially, the same as endorse.

clue.text: Spare home converted for communication system

indicators.note: a conversion turns something into a different form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A spare house is converted to serve as a communications centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Semaphore is a signalling system using flags or arms held in set positions.

clue.text: Parking burden for domestic technician

parts.note: P is the road-sign symbol for parking
to lumber someone is to burden them with a task

explanation.surface: Finding a parking space is a burden for a tradesman visiting a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A plumber is a tradesman who fits and repairs water pipes in homes.

clue.text: Dash before day to find ruminant

parts.note: elan is dash or flair
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Someone rushes off before the day starts to track down a grazing animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' puts ELAN ahead of D.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope, and like all antelopes it chews the cud.

clue.text: Assign a set of things at Sotheby's, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the answer matches the sound

parts.words: a set of things at Sotheby's
parts.note: an item or bundle offered at an auction house is a lot

explanation.surface: Someone allocates a batch of items at the auction house, by all accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: Sotheby's is a famous auction house, where each item for sale is a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to assign or give out a share to someone.

clue.text: Not half rude piece DJ played showing bias

indicators.note: something played is performed in a new way, so the letters are rearranged
not half means losing half, so the back half of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A radio DJ plays a fairly offensive track, showing bias.
explanation.walkthrough: RUDE loses DE to leave RU, which is mixed with PIECE and DJ.
explanation.definitionFit: Prejudice is a preconceived bias for or against someone.

clue.text: Key figure in view of bigwig being raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something lifts it so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: 'to me' means in my view, so in the view of is to
a VIP is a very important person

explanation.surface: A central person, as an important figure sees it, is promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: TO and VIP are read upwards together.
explanation.definitionFit: A pivot is the central point things turn on, so a key person in a team or plan.

clue.text: Moral system from old character in charge

parts.note: eth is an Old English letter
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A set of values handed down from a veteran figure in authority.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a set of moral principles, such as the work ethic.

clue.text: Mogul's centre in unusually variable London area

indicators.note: being in something means going inside the other letters
unusually means not in the usual way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter only

parts.note: the middle letter of the five

explanation.surface: A tycoon at the heart of a volatile property district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: VARIABLE is rearranged and G slipped inside. Belgravia is a wealthy district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgravia is an affluent residential district of London near Hyde Park.

clue.text: Captain from home country missing final pair

indicators.note: missing the final pair means the last two letters are taken away

parts.note: Blighty is old British slang for Britain, used by soldiers abroad

explanation.surface: A naval captain hails from his home country but lacks his final pair of something.
explanation.walkthrough: BLIGHTY drops TY. William Bligh was the captain of HMS Bounty when its crew mutinied.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain William Bligh commanded the Bounty, famous for the 1789 mutiny.

clue.text: Ask bridge players to come with doctor

parts.note: East and North are two of the four partners at bridge
to doctor someone is to treat them

explanation.surface: Someone invites card players to come along with a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to ask earnestly, to beg or plead.

clue.text: Irregular American at heart protecting strikebreaker

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so one piece goes around the other
the heart of a word is its middle, so the outer letters are shed

parts.note: the middle four letters of the eight
a rat is someone who works during a strike, a scab

explanation.surface: An irregular picture of an American shielding someone who crosses a picket line.
explanation.walkthrough: A rat is slang for someone who works while colleagues are on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means unpredictable or inconsistent, so not regular.
